title: Chapter 228: The Devil's Story
html:
Han Qiuming managed a single shout before something clamped over his mouth. Terror swallowed him whole. Unable to see clearly, he felt an icy sensation surge through his body as something carried him away. A door closed, and the corridor returned to its former state.

The Third Sick Hall was vast, its corridors separated by considerable distances, yet Ye Xiaoxin still heard the commotion. After a moment’s hesitation, she left the director’s office. Brave though she was, she placed each step with care. She rounded the corner and found nothing.

Where did that man disappear to? Did he trigger a trap?Ye Xiaoxin continued down the dark corridor.

Footsteps suddenly echoed ahead. Han Qiuming’s steps are light and unsteady. These are firm and powerful—the steps of someone who knows exactly where he’s going.

Ye Xiaoxin slipped into a nearby sickroom and peered through the crack beside the door.

A terrifying monster soon emerged. He wore a bloodstained doctor’s coat, and his face looked stitched together. A murderous aura surrounded him, and he carried a grotesque hammer spattered with blood. Its head scraped across the floor. It resembled no prop, but a genuine murder weapon.

The actor inside the Third Sick Hall? The actor only appears after twenty minutes?

Ye Xiaoxin had lost her composure only once before, when she saw the figure clinging to Han Qiuming’s back. Now it happened again. As the monster advanced, her pale fingers tightened around the door. No other Haunted House had made her feel this way, and she could not understand why.

Why am I so afraid?The monster handled the hammer with practiced ease, and every instinct urged Ye Xiaoxin to hide. Actors in other Haunted Houses are obviously performing. But this doctor looks as though he has truly done something unspeakable with that hammer.

Only after the doctor had passed did Ye Xiaoxin silently emerge. She jotted a few brief words in her notebook, then began following him.

…

In the deepest reaches of the Third Sick Hall, Guo Miao and Song An stood outside Room 10.

“The numbering in this corridor differs from the others. Rooms 8, 9, and 10 are especially unusual—their doors are made of steel.”

Guo Miao shared his observations with the others. “We should focus on these three rooms. Keep one another in sight. If you find anything, call for help, and don’t touch it alone.”

The group entered Room 8 first. Security mesh covered the window, and restraint straps hung from both sides of the steel bed. Something about the entire room felt wrong, though the reason was not obvious at first glance.

“This room...” Guo Miao studied the bed for a long time before saying uncertainly, “Everything seems asymmetrical.”

Once he pointed it out, the others noticed it too. Half the wardrobe had been destroyed while the other half remained perfectly intact. The bed’s left side was undamaged, but its right was badly twisted. Even the floor was clean on one side and filthy on the other. “What is this room supposed to mean? Is asymmetry the clue to clearing the scenario?”

Room 8 had housed Xiong Qing, a patient with hemineglect. What appeared balanced to an ordinary person looked distorted from his perspective. To him, the world itself was warped and diseased—and therefore needed correction. The group searched Room 8 for a long time but found nothing. They moved on to Room 9.

Room 9 was the cleanest in the Third Sick Hall. It contained no trash, and no strange drawings marred the walls. In this place, however, such cleanliness only made the room more disturbing. The group searched it without success.

“What is Boss Chen trying to convey? This design is difficult to understand.” Room 9’s patient had been Wu Fei, a man whom even Men Nan’s primary personality considered dangerous.

When they opened the final steel door, a pungent stench assaulted everyone outside. Their hair stood on end, and they prepared to flee.

During Chen Ge’s Trial Mission, Room 10 had been locked, so he had never seen the real room’s interior.

“Should we leave?” Su Luoluo asked outside the door with her hand over her nose.

“The smell isn’t as strong inside, but you and Xiao Du can wait out here.” Guo Miao and Song An entered Room 10. Its interior could only be described as madness. It had no windows and was completely enclosed. There was neither a bed nor furniture of any kind—only several decaying, foul-smelling mattresses scattered across the floor.

When Guo Miao and Song An turned toward the walls, even they recoiled. Bloody messages of every size covered every surface, overlapping so densely that the writing seemed to writhe.

Most frightening of all was the man’s face embedded in the wall opposite the door. It was little more than a thin layer, its expression suspended somewhere between a smile and a grimace.

“Boss, that face doesn’t look like a prop. Artificial rubber couldn’t create an effect like this.”

“I know.”

Guo Miao took several steps toward the face and raised a hand to test it. Still several feet away, however, he could force himself no closer. “Forget it. I doubt the clue involves the face. It’s probably hidden among the bloody writing.”

Guo Miao studied the words surrounding the face. Unlike the messages in the corridor, these sentences followed a basic logic, as though they told a story. Shining his phone on the wall, he read aloud.

“My wife accused me of being a murderer. My parents refused to speak to me. The neighbors pointed and whispered. Everyone abandoned me.

“I shouldn’t be alive, yet I can find no reason to die. I killed my own children. Yes, I have never denied it.

“I shouldn’t have left them home alone. I shouldn’t have left the stove burning while I rushed to work.

“Three lives, three children.

“What can I do to earn salvation?

“I want to tear out my heart and show it to you.

“Please stop blaming me. I’m sorry. Everything was my fault.

“I shouldn’t have argued. I should have accepted my mistake in silence. If I hadn’t fought with my wife that night, perhaps she wouldn’t have left so late to visit her parents, and those people would never have harmed her.

“I’m sorry, this is all my fault.

“I want to atone for my sins, but who would accept my penance?

“There is a needle inside me, poised above my heart. Every breath drives it deeper.

“What can I do? Try my best to live.

“I moved somewhere entirely new, but nothing changed.

“Guilt torments me. I am a killer, an unforgivable killer.”
